correctness.rationale: Each non-backtracking petal excursion returns to the hub, and the petal label has same-state probability 1/(2k-1) and any distinct-state probability 2/(2k-1). Given r distinct petals seen, next new-petal probability p_r=2(k-r)/(2k-1) yields independent geometric waiting times for coupon completion J; exact cover time is weighted excursion length sum minus one final untraversed return edge. Exchangeability gives E C_i=E J/k, and a two-state marked-petal recurrence evaluates transverse occupation-count covariance eigenvalue b_k. Orthogonal covariance decomposition yields variance L²Var(J)/k²+b_k(Q-L²/k). Because b_k>0, integer unit smoothing strictly reduces variance until lengths differ by <=1. Independent first-principles directed-edge/visited-vertex rational Markov-chain moments agreed for six bouquets, including k=2,3,4.

value.rationale: Separating mean invariance from strict variance sensitivity is a motivated exact stochastic-graph phenomenon: fixed number of cycles and total length give identical expected cover time but quantitatively different risk. The sharp balancing rule is useful in designing finite bouquet networks and interprets memory effects of the non-backtracking walk.

final_claim: For a hub-start non-backtracking walk on bouquet of k>=2 simple cycles of lengths ell_i>=3, exact vertex cover-time mean E[T]=L m_k/k-1 and variance L² v_k/k²+b_k(Q-L²/k), with m_k=1+(2k-1)H_(k-1)/2, v_k=(2k-1)^2 H_(k-1)^(2)/4-(2k-1)H_(k-1)/2, b_k=1/k+(2k-1)(k-2)H_(k-1)/(2k(k-1))>0; balancing lengths minimizes variance strictly.
